OTP input

A one-time code, one box per character, posted as one field. Every box is drawn from the input’s own recipe.

The boxes carry no name. A hidden input carries the joined code, so the form posts code=482193 and nothing else. Typing, pasting and the browser’s autofill need the package’s script; the gallery loads none, so what is here is the server’s render.

Copy button

A ds::button that copies a value and confirms in place. Both labels sit in one cell from the first paint, so the button is as wide as “Copied” before anything is pressed and never jumps.

Copying needs the package’s script; the gallery loads none, so these are the server’s render, at rest. A refused clipboard changes nothing on the button and dispatches copy-failed instead.
Variants and sizes · secondary by default
Icon only, and beside what it copies · target reads the element at the moment of the press

Swap button

A button that answers in place: “Save” becomes “Saved”, “Follow” becomes “Following”. Both faces share one grid cell from the first paint, so the button is as wide as the wider face and never jumps. The copy button runs on the same recipe.

Swapping needs the package’s script; the gallery loads none, so each pair below is the server’s render, at rest and with swapped set. revert="0" makes a toggle with aria-pressed; any other value swaps back after that many milliseconds.
Toggle · revert="0", at rest and swapped
Confirmation after a save · event swaps when the host says the save worked, not on the press

Rating

Stars that are radios underneath: one name, one value posted, the arrow keys and the form’s required check for free. Hovering previews “up to here” and leaving restores the choice, all in CSS. Readonly is one image, named “4.5 out of 5”.

No script at all. The faint cross after the stars is “No rating”, the way back once a star is chosen; it is transparent while it is itself the choice, and omitted when the rating is required.

Chip group

Pressable filters. Each chip is a real radio or checkbox under a pill, so the group posts with the form and binds with wire:model on the group. Or each is a link, for filtering by URL. A chosen chip opens a check before its words, by a width transition, so the row slides rather than jumps.

No script. ds::badge is the static pill; this is the one you press. A group is all inputs or all links, never both, and says so when the view renders.

Segmented control

One of a few views or modes, side by side in a track. Each segment is a real radio, so the control posts with the form, takes the arrow keys and binds with wire:model on the control. Or each is a link, for switching views by URL.

No script needed. With the package's script and Alpine, one highlight slides between segments; this page loads no Alpine, so what you see is the face CSS draws on the chosen segment, which is also what every page shows before the script runs.

Button group

Related buttons joined into one shape: the inner corners square off and neighbouring borders become one line. The group sets the size and variant of the buttons inside it, and any button can still set its own.

No script. A split button is a group whose last member is a ds::dropdown with a button as its trigger; the dropdown itself needs Alpine, the group does not.
Outlined · secondary, the default, at sm, md, lg
Split button and filled · primary, danger, parted by a hairline

Expanding · expanding: icons whose labels open on hover, keyboard focus, and while pressed or current
Home Inbox Calendar Settings
The group fills its container, so a label opening never moves what sits beside it. Hover the others; Tab to them. On a phone there is no hover, so only the pressed or current one is open, and every button keeps its label as its name.

Icon swap

Two icons that turn into each other — menu and close, play and pause, sun and moon — by crossfading, rotating or flipping two stacked icons, plus a three-bar menu drawn from spans that folds into a cross. No path morphing.

No script. The swap reads the state of the button around it — aria-expanded, aria-pressed, aria-checked or data-state — so a dropdown trigger or a drawer button turns its icon by itself. Each row below is the same buttons with that attribute off, then on. With reduced motion it switches instantly.
Presets · menu, crossfade, rotate, rotate, flip, and a lone chevron that turns

Toolbar

A row of tools that is one stop in the tab order: the arrow keys move between its buttons, Home and End jump to the ends. With the script, a highlight follows the pointer and the keyboard from button to button, and darkens while one is pressed.

Needs Alpine and the package's script for the keyboard and the highlight. This page loads no Alpine, so the buttons show their static faces; the pressed ones are drawn from PHP.

Toggle group

Buttons that stay pressed. single is a radio group: one is on, and pressing another moves it. multiple is a set of on/off buttons. With a name it posts like the radios or checkboxes it stands in for.

Radio cards

Options big enough to compare: plans, shipping methods. The whole card is the label of a real, visible radio, so the arrow keys, required and posting are the browser’s. The chosen card is ringed by :has(:checked); no ring slides between them.

No script. The name a screen reader hears is the title and the meta (“Pro, $12 a month”); the description and body are read after it. Every column count collapses to one on a phone.

Tag input

Short values typed into a field and kept as removable chips. Each chip carries the hidden input it posts, so what is on screen and what is submitted cannot disagree.

An entry that cannot be added stays in the box with a message under it, in the help line’s place. Nothing typed is ever dropped. The gallery loads no script, so the chips here are the server’s.

Number field

A native type=number with decrease and increase buttons. The arrow keys and typing are the browser’s; the buttons add a press, a hold that repeats, and a stop at each bound.

The buttons are out of the tab order on purpose: a keyboard already has the arrow keys. A button at its bound is disabled by the server’s render, before any script runs.

Password: reveal and strength

reveal on ds::input adds a show/hide toggle; ds::password-strength is a meter bound to the field by its id. The score is a hint for the person typing, not a security control.

The level is spoken in words through a polite live region and shown by how many bars are lit, never by colour alone. The gallery loads no script, so the meter here is empty; the documentation image shows it scored.

Sub-nav

A rail item that holds the pages belonging to it. The children are ordinary nav items, indented under a guide line.

Two different facts, two different marks: the page you are on is the raised card; the section it sits in is drawn at full strength, no card. The open and closed states are rendered by the server, which is why this page shows them without Alpine.

Dropdown

A menu of verbs anchored to the control that opened it. Not a select — a select holds values and posts them; this holds actions and performs them.

Elevation is float, not overlay. The shadow scale is where the system says whether a surface hovers over the page or blocks it, and this one hovers.
The gallery loads no Alpine, so every menu here renders open. That is the state worth reviewing anyway — the closed state is just the trigger.

A small panel of anything, anchored to the button that opened it: filters, a share form, a few settings. A non-modal dialog — the dropdown stays a menu.

The gallery loads no Alpine, so these panels stay closed: they are x-cloaked until Alpine shows them, and placed by the package's script. The open panel, flipped and on screen, is in the documentation screenshot and driven by the behaviour suite.

A full-width banner above the app’s chrome: maintenance, a trial ending, a new feature. A landmark, not a live region, unless an outage is marked urgent.

Progress

A task with a known length, or one without. The fill reads one number, --ds-progress, so a host moves it with a single binding and no class is ever built at runtime.

The indeterminate sweep is motion-safe. Ask for reduced motion and it becomes a static striped bar — a still partial bar would read as a real value.

The active underline is fg, not accent. A tab row is structure, not a link — colouring the active one accent makes the inactive tabs look like the links.

Toast

Surface with a border, not the alert’s tinted wash: it floats over unknown content and has to paint an opaque ground. The tone lives in the icon alone, so four stacked toasts do not become a colour chart.

The region is rendered always, and empty most of the time. A live region only announces content that arrives after it is in the document — render it with the first toast and the first toast is silent.

Switch

A setting that takes effect. role="switch" makes a screen reader say “on” and “off” — “unchecked”, for a setting that is simply off, reads as a form the reader failed to fill in.

The label sits left and the control right, the opposite of the checkbox: a switch is one of a list of settings the reader scans down the left edge.

Accordion

Sections that expand one at a time. The one component in the system that holds state — exclusivity is a relationship between items, so no single item can enforce it.

A collapsed panel is visibility: hidden, not overflow: hidden. That takes its content out of the tab order AND the accessibility tree; a collapsed section whose links are still tabbable is the classic broken accordion, and it looks perfect.

Date picker

A calendar for one date or a range. Every value is a Y-m-d string, never a Date — new Date('2026-03-29') is UTC midnight, which west of Greenwich is the 28th.

A range posts two fields. Two dates are two values, and squeezing them into one string means every consumer writing the same parser.
Range · endpoints inverse, the span washed — shown open

File upload

A styled file field with drag-and-drop and local previews. It does not upload anything — progress needs somewhere to upload to, and that is a backend contract nothing else here has.

The real <input type="file"> is stretched over the whole zone at zero opacity, so the entire area is the control and drag-and-drop lands on the element that owns the files.
Drop zone · the accept string is rendered for a person: image/*,.pdf becomes “images, PDF”

Slider

One value or a range on a track. Every thumb is a native input type="range", so the keyboard, the screen reader and the post are the browser's; the track and the fill are drawn around them.

The fill is rendered from PHP, so here, with no script, it is in the right place. It is the script that keeps it in step while a thumb moves.

Time picker

A time typed the way people type times, or picked from a list. It posts HH:MM in 24 hours whatever it shows.

This is the field without the script: the browser's own input type="time", with the same name, bounds and step. The script turns it into a text field with a list of times.

Inline edit

Text that turns into a field where it stands, in the font of where it sits. Enter saves, Escape puts it back.

With no script there is no text to press: each is a plain field, named and posting in the form around it, and with action inside a form it draws, with a Save and a Cancel (the form's reset). The script hides the field behind the text until it is pressed.
Without the script · in a heading, with action, a failed save

Use letters, numbers and dashes.

Scroll area

A box that scrolls natively within a height, with a thin scrollbar in the tokens' colours and a shadow at each edge that has more past it.

No script here and none needed: the shadows are scroll-driven CSS. A box of plain text is a Tab stop of its own, a named region, so a keyboard can scroll it.

Command palette

Actions and destinations, searched from a shortcut (Cmd+K or Ctrl+K), in the modal's layer. Focus stays in the field; the arrows move through the options and Enter runs one.

The palette is on this page, closed: it opens only with Alpine and the package's script, which the gallery does not load, and without them it stays closed and does nothing. Below is the trigger recipe from its docs; the open palette is in the documentation screenshot.

Sortable list

Rows put in order by dragging a handle, from the keyboard, or with Move up and Move down. The order posts as name[].

Without the script this is what a reader gets: the rows in the server's order, posting that order, with no handles (a handle that did nothing would be worse than none). The script adds the handles and the buttons.
Without the script · three steps, the last one fixed
  • Write the brief
  • Review the draft
  • Ship it

Press Space or Enter to pick it up, the arrow keys to move it, Space or Enter to drop it, Escape to cancel.

Split

Panes with a divider to drag between them; here a vertical split nested in a horizontal one. Sizes are CSS variables written by PHP, so the first paint is the final one.

With no script the panes stay at their sizes and the dividers are plain lines, which is what this page shows. The script makes each divider a focusable separator you can drag or move with the arrow keys.

Tokens

Every token names a job, not a colour. Both themes are shown side by side because that is the only way drift between them is visible.

surface the card content sits on
surface-sunken the ground behind it
surface-subtle table heads, row hover
surface-inverse primary buttons, the FAB
border the default hairline
border-strong a card edge that must read as raised
fg headings
fg-body running copy
fg-muted labels, meta, timestamps
fg-subtle icons that repeat an adjacent label
accent links
success success
warning warning
danger danger
fg-subtle is 2.63:1 on the card in light — below the 3:1 a meaningful mark needs. It is allowed only where the information is also written next to it. Timestamps are not redundant, so they use fg-muted.
